1	name: packslip
     2	description: >
     3	  Publish a signed packslip for a release: attest the artifacts' build
     4	  provenance, digest them, sign the release manifest keylessly with this
     5	  job's OIDC identity, and upload the bundle as a release asset.
     6	author: Jeff Dickey <@jdx>
     7	branding:
     8	  icon: package
     9	  color: red
    10	
    11	inputs:
    12	  artifacts:
    13	    description: >
    14	      Artifact files or globs already present locally, whitespace separated
    15	      (dist/*.tar.xz dist/*.zip). At least one file must match between this
    16	      and `download`.
    17	    required: false
    18	    default: ""
    19	  download:
    20	    description: >
    21	      Release asset name patterns to fetch before collecting artifacts,
    22	      whitespace separated (mytool-*.tar.gz mytool-*.zip). Downloaded files
    23	      join `artifacts`, so a job whose archives already live on the release
    24	      named by `tag` needs no separate `gh release download` step, and no
    25	      second copy of these patterns for a local artifacts glob.
    26	    required: false
    27	    default: ""
    28	  project:
    29	    description: >
    30	      The project's name; defaults to github.com/<owner>/<repo>. A tool in
    31	      a monorepo names itself github.com/<owner>/<repo>/<tool> and runs this
    32	      step once per tool.
    33	    required: false
    34	    default: ""
    35	  version:
    36	    description: The release version; defaults to the tag name without a leading v
    37	    required: false
    38	    default: ""
    39	  tag:
    40	    description: The release tag to upload to; defaults to the tag that triggered the job
    41	    required: false
    42	    default: ""
    43	  url-base:
    44	    description: Download URL prefix; defaults to this release's download URL
    45	    required: false
    46	    default: ""
    47	  bin:
    48	    description: >
    49	      Executables inside every artifact, whitespace separated, each a path
    50	      relative to the archive root or NAME=PATH when the PATH name differs.
    51	      A plain name is looked up inside each archive, so `tool` finds
    52	      `tool-1.2.3-linux-x64/tool`; for a bare executable it is the name the
    53	      file gets on PATH.
    54	    required: false
    55	    default: ""
    56	  manifest:
    57	    description: >
    58	      A TOML manifest (`packslip create --manifest`) for what the inputs
    59	      cannot say per artifact: executables at different paths in different
    60	      archives, a format the file name gets wrong, host requirements, an
    61	      artifact that runs anywhere, and resources. Artifacts it lists are
    62	      merged with the `artifacts` input.
    63	    required: false
    64	    default: ""
    65	  variants:
    66	    description: >
    67	      Variants for artifacts that share a platform, as FILENAME=VARIANT,
    68	      whitespace separated (tool-fips-linux-x64.tar.gz=fips).
    69	    required: false
    70	    default: ""
    71	  formats:
    72	    description: >
    73	      The format of an artifact whose name does not say, as FILENAME=FORMAT,
    74	      whitespace separated (tool-linux-x64.bin=raw). Every artifact needs
    75	      one; the name gives it for the usual archive, installer, and bare
    76	      executable spellings, and this is for the rest.
    77	    required: false
    78	    default: ""
    79	  resources:
    80	    description: >
    81	      What ships besides the executables, one per line, each a `packslip
    82	      create --resource` value: KIND[/QUALIFIER][@os[/arch[/libc]]]=SOURCE:VALUE,
    83	      where the optional @ scope limits an entry to one platform
    84	      (man@linux=archive:share/man/man1/tool.1), such as
    85	      completion/zsh=archive:share/zsh/site-functions/_tool,
    86	      man=archive:share/man/man1/tool.1, cli-spec/usage=exec:tool usage,
    87	      skill/tool=repo:skills/tool, skill/tool=asset:dist/tool-skill.tar.gz,
    88	      or sbom/cyclonedx=asset:dist/tool.cdx.json (an asset is a file
    89	      digested alongside the artifacts; one the artifacts glob also matched
    90	      is treated as the asset, not an artifact).
    91	    required: false
    92	    default: ""
    93	  require:
    94	    description: >
    95	      Commands the executables need on PATH, one per line, each a `packslip
    96	      create --require` value: bin:NAME or bin:NAME@MIN, such as bin:java@17.
    97	      What the executables load from the host is read from them and needs
    98	      no input.
    99	    required: false
   100	    default: ""
   101	  notes-url:
   102	    description: URL of the release notes; defaults to the release page
   103	    required: false
   104	    default: ""
   105	  extensions:
   106	    description: >
   107	      Release-level extensions, one per line, each a `packslip create
   108	      --extension` value: NAME=JSON, where NAME is who defines the value (a
   109	      consumer such as mise, or a domain the vendor controls) and JSON is
   110	      the value, such as example.com={"build_id":"20260901.3"}.
   111	    required: false
   112	    default: ""
   113	  attest:
   114	    description: >
   115	      What to do about build provenance. `true` attests every artifact with
   116	      actions/attest-build-provenance and links the attestation from the
   117	      packslip, and needs the attestations: write permission. `link` only
   118	      links it, for a workflow whose build jobs already attested the files
   119	      as they produced them; it needs no extra permission, and an artifact
   120	      nothing attested leaves a URL that resolves to nothing. `false` does
   121	      neither.
   122	    required: false
   123	    default: "true"
   124	  out:
   125	    description: Directory to write the bundle into
   126	    required: false
   127	    default: packslip
   128	  upload:
   129	    description: Upload the packslip to the release
   130	    required: false
   131	    default: "true"
   132	  packslip-version:
   133	    description: >
   134	      The packslip release to run; defaults to the version this action was
   135	      released with (read from its Cargo.toml). Ignored when packslip-path
   136	      is set.
   137	    required: false
   138	    default: ""
   139	  packslip-path:
   140	    description: >
   141	      An existing packslip executable to run instead of downloading a
   142	      release: a path, or a name to look up on PATH. For a platform with no
   143	      release asset the job can run, build the CLI first (`cargo install
   144	      packslip --locked --root "$RUNNER_TEMP/packslip"`) and point this at
   145	      it. The action runs the binary as given and does not check its
   146	      provenance, so the job is responsible for where it came from.
   147	    required: false
   148	    default: ""
   149	  token:
   150	    description: Token for downloading packslip and uploading assets
   151	    required: false
   152	    default: ${{ github.token }}
   153	
   154	outputs:
   155	  bundle:
   156	    description: Path of the written bundle
   157	    value: ${{ steps.create.outputs.bundle }}
   158	
   159	runs:
   160	  using: composite
   161	  steps:
   162	    - name: Install packslip
   163	      shell: bash
   164	      env:
   165	        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
   166	        PACKSLIP_VERSION: ${{ inputs.packslip-version }}
   167	        PACKSLIP_PATH: ${{ inputs.packslip-path }}
   168	        PACKSLIP_ACTION_ROOT: ${{ github.action_path }}
   169	      run: bash "$PACKSLIP_ACTION_ROOT/scripts/install-packslip.sh"
   170	
   171	    - name: Download release assets
   172	      id: download
   173	      if: inputs.download != ''
   174	      shell: bash
   175	      env:
   176	        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
   177	        IN_DOWNLOAD: ${{ inputs.download }}
   178	        IN_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
   179	        REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
   180	        REF_TYPE: ${{ github.ref_type }}
   181	        REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
   182	      run: |
   183	        set -euo pipefail
   184	        # IN_DOWNLOAD holds asset-name globs for `gh release download
   185	        # --pattern`, not paths to expand against this job's working
   186	        # directory -- turn off pathname expansion so a pattern like *.zip
   187	        # is never quietly replaced by whatever it happens to match here.
   188	        set -f
   189	        tag="${IN_TAG:-$REF_NAME}"
   190	        if [ -z "$IN_TAG" ] && [ "$REF_TYPE" != tag ]; then
   191	          echo "download is set but not running on a tag; pass the tag input" >&2
   192	          exit 1
   193	        fi
   194	        # A fresh directory per invocation, not a fixed name: the monorepo
   195	        # flow calls this action once per tool in the same job, and a fixed
   196	        # name would still hold the previous tool's files when this step is
   197	        # skipped for one of them.
   198	        dir="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP}/packslip-download.XXXXXX")"
   199	        args=(--repo "$REPO" --dir "$dir" --clobber)
   200	        for pattern in $IN_DOWNLOAD; do
   201	          args+=(--pattern "$pattern")
   202	        done
   203	        gh release download "$tag" "${args[@]}"
   204	        echo "dir=$dir" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   205	
   206	    - name: Collect artifacts
   207	      id: files
   208	      shell: bash
   209	      env:
   210	        IN_ARTIFACTS: ${{ inputs.artifacts }}
   211	        IN_DOWNLOAD: ${{ inputs.download }}
   212	        IN_DOWNLOAD_DIR: ${{ steps.download.outputs.dir }}
   213	      run: |
   214	        set -euo pipefail
   215	        shopt -s nullglob
   216	        files=()
   217	        for pattern in $IN_ARTIFACTS; do
   218	          for f in $pattern; do [ -f "$f" ] && files+=("$f"); done
   219	        done
   220	        if [ -n "$IN_DOWNLOAD_DIR" ]; then
   221	          # Listed, not glob-matched: on a Windows runner RUNNER_TEMP is a
   222	          # backslash path, which bash's pathname expansion would otherwise
   223	          # read as glob escapes and match nothing.
   224	          while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
   225	            files+=("$f")
   226	          done < <(find "$IN_DOWNLOAD_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0)
   227	        fi
   228	        if [ "${#files[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
   229	          echo "no artifacts matched: artifacts=[$IN_ARTIFACTS] download=[$IN_DOWNLOAD]" >&2
   230	          exit 1
   231	        fi
   232	        printf '%s\n' "${files[@]}" > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/packslip-files"
   233	        {
   234	          echo 'files<<EOF'
   235	          printf '%s\n' "${files[@]}"
   236	          echo 'EOF'
   237	        } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   238	
   239	    - name: Check the provenance mode
   240	      shell: bash

   172	      id: download
   173	      if: inputs.download != ''

   175	      env:
   176	        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.token }}
   177	        IN_DOWNLOAD: ${{ inputs.download }}
   178	        IN_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
   179	        REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
   180	        REF_TYPE: ${{ github.ref_type }}
   181	        REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

   236	          echo 'EOF'
   237	        } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

The discussion’s diagnosis is correct. Two separate failures compounded:

1. **Immediate CI failure:** hk pinned `jdx/packslip@v1.0.1` to a SHA, but that composite action internally used `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` without a full SHA. hk’s GitHub Actions policy rejected that nested action while preparing `create-release`. The [release run](https://github.com/jdx/hk/actions/runs/33982465558) shows every build succeeding, then `create-release` failing at “Set up job”—before any release step executed.

2. **Release bookkeeping failure:** the `v1.58.0` tag and changelog entry already existed before publishing began. Because `create-release` never ran:

   - no GitHub release or draft was created;
   - `cargo publish` was skipped;
   - release-note enhancement and final publication were skipped.

The dependency was corrected in [PR #1335](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1335): packslip `v1.1.1` pins the nested provenance action to a full SHA. Then `v1.58.1` released successfully.

The remaining missing-notes problem happened because release generation treats **the previous Git tag**, not the previous successfully published release, as its boundary. Therefore `v1.58.1` compared `v1.58.0...v1.58.1`; it had no reason to include the changes already assigned to the dead `v1.58.0` tag.

Why pre-release checks missed it: hk’s workflow visibly pinned packslip correctly, and the nested violation lived inside the external composite action. The repository’s policy only exposed it when GitHub expanded that action during the real release job.

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

item.stdout:
This release seeds hk with an embedded Pkl package so matching-version configs validate offline on a cold cache, adds templated `dir` support for workspace-aware steps, and lands a new `check_after_diff` mechanism that lets partial fixers (like ShellCheck) apply what they can while still reporting what they cannot. It also brings several new Go and lint builtins plus a batch of correctness fixes for Go linters, gitleaks, workspace paths, Windows shims, and stashing.

## Added

- **Embedded matching-version Pkl package** (@sahidvelji) [#1218](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1218). hk now ships the Pkl package built for its own version and seeds `HK_PKL_CACHE_DIR` with it before evaluating `hk.pkl`, so a config pinned to that version validates with no network round trip on a cold cache — a fresh clone, CI runner, new container, or upgrade. Cached content always wins over the embedded copy, and other versions are fetched as before. Set `HK_PKL_EMBEDDED=0` to disable seeding. Addresses [discussion #1216](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1216).

- **Templated `dir` through Tera** (@sahidvelji) [#1219](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1219). A step's `dir` is now rendered through Tera, so a workspace-aware step can point its working directory at the workspace it was matched for instead of prefixing every command with `cd {{workspace}} && ...`. The eight workspace-aware builtins (the Go ones plus `cargo_deny`) drop their `cd` prefix as a result. Literal `dir` values are unaffected.

  ```pkl
  ["go-vet"] {
    glob = "**/*.go"
    workspace_indicator = "go.mod"
    dir = "{{workspace}}"
    check = "go vet ./..."
  }
  ```

- **`check_after_diff` for partial fixers** (@jdx) [#1243](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1243). New opt-in step setting that reruns `check` on the original file batch after a `check_diff` patch applies, so non-fixable findings stay visible instead of being masked by a clean apply. Requires both `check` and `check_diff` to be defined. This underpins ShellCheck's new fixer and other partial fixers.

- **ShellCheck autofix via `check_diff`** (@sahidvelji) [#1237](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1237). `shellcheck` now applies the fixes it can via `--format=diff`, and thanks to `check_after_diff` a file with both fixable and non-fixable findings is fixed and still fails on what remains. Implements proposal 2 of [#1234](https://github.com/jdx/hk/issues/1234).

- **`go_fix` builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1224](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1224). Wraps Go's `go fix` (the Go 1.26+ analyzer-driven modernizer) — `interface{}` → `any`, `sort.Slice` → `slices.Sort`, `wg.Add`/`go`/`wg.Done` → `wg.Go`, and more. `check_diff` runs `go fix -diff ./...` and hk applies the patch directly. Requires Go 1.26+.

- **`golangci_lint_fmt` formatter builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1244](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1244). Wraps `golangci-lint fmt`, the formatter half of golangci-lint, formatting only the changed files via `check_diff` (using `fmt --diff`) — separate from the existing `golangci_lint` builtin that runs the full linter.

- **`ls_lint` builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1238](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1238). Adds a builtin for [ls-lint](https://ls-lint.org), which enforces directory and filename naming conventions against `.ls-lint.yml`. Runs once per invocation. Implements proposal 3 of [#1234](https://github.com/jdx/hk/issues/1234).

- **`gitleaks_staged` builtin** (@jdx) [#1248](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1248). A new builtin that runs `gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged` to scan only the staged index, suited to pre-commit hooks.

- **Per-step `allow_failure`** (@jdx) [#1291](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1291). Steps can report a non-zero command exit without failing the overall hook, including conditional policies via expressions such as `env('KNOWN_BROKEN') == 'true'`. hk's own execution and configuration errors remain blocking, and allowed failures are surfaced in structured output.

## Fixed

- **Go linters that reported success on bad code** (@sahidvelji) [#1225](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1225). `go_imports`, `go_lines`, `revive`, and `go_fumpt` silently passed in check mode even with real findings; they now take their exit code correctly. `gomod_tidy` could not run outside the repo root and is now scoped like the other Go builtins.
- **gitleaks scan modes** (@jdx) [#1248](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1248). `Builtins.gitleaks` now explicitly scans the repository working tree rather than silently changing behavior when `{{files}}` expanded to multiple paths.
- **`gomod_tidy` now runs on `.go` changes** (@sahidvelji) [#1236](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1236). Broadened the glob to `**/*.go`, `**/go.mod`, and `**/go.sum` so the common drift (editing an import) is caught at commit time, and its `go.mod`/`go.sum` updates are now staged when triggered by a Go change (@jdx) [#1240](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1240).
- **Partial diff fixes no longer pass silently** (@jdx) [#1245](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1245). Enabled `check_after_diff` for `rumdl`, `ryl`, `ryl_markdown`, `zizmor`, and `pinact_v3`, so remaining violations surface after hk applies each partial patch.
- **Workspace paths in literal `dir` steps** (@jdx) [#1242](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1242). `{{workspace}}` and `{{workspace_indicator}}` are now rendered relative to a literal step directory, preventing duplicated paths like `ui/ui/tsconfig.json` in subprojects. Addresses [discussion #1233](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1233).
- **Windows command shims** (@jdx) [#1221](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1221). Structured `argv` steps now resolve `.cmd`/`.bat` targets (including npm `node_modules/.bin` shims) via the effective `PATH`/`PATHEXT` and run them through `cmd.exe` with argument-boundary-preserving escaping. Fixes [discussion #1220](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1220).
- **Empty pathspec stashes** (@jdx) [#1283](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1283). Cached content always wins over the embedded copy, and other versions are fetched as before. Set `HK_PKL_EMBEDDED=0` to disable seeding. Addresses [discussion #1216](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1216).

- **Templated `dir` through Tera** (@sahidvelji) [#1219](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1219). A step's `dir` is now rendered through Tera, so a workspace-aware step can point its working directory at the workspace it was matched for instead of prefixing every command with `cd {{workspace}} && ...`. The eight workspace-aware builtins (the Go ones plus `cargo_deny`) drop their `cd` prefix as a result. Literal `dir` values are unaffected.

  ```pkl
  ["go-vet"] {
    glob = "**/*.go"
    workspace_indicator = "go.mod"
    dir = "{{workspace}}"
    check = "go vet ./..."
  }
  ```

- **`check_after_diff` for partial fixers** (@jdx) [#1243](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1243). New opt-in step setting that reruns `check` on the original file batch after a `check_diff` patch applies, so non-fixable findings stay visible instead of being masked by a clean apply. Requires both `check` and `check_diff` to be defined. This underpins ShellCheck's new fixer and other partial fixers.

- **ShellCheck autofix via `check_diff`** (@sahidvelji) [#1237](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1237). `shellcheck` now applies the fixes it can via `--format=diff`, and thanks to `check_after_diff` a file with both fixable and non-fixable findings is fixed and still fails on what remains. Implements proposal 2 of [#1234](https://github.com/jdx/hk/issues/1234).

- **`go_fix` builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1224](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1224). Wraps Go's `go fix` (the Go 1.26+ analyzer-driven modernizer) — `interface{}` → `any`, `sort.Slice` → `slices.Sort`, `wg.Add`/`go`/`wg.Done` → `wg.Go`, and more. `check_diff` runs `go fix -diff ./...` and hk applies the patch directly. Requires Go 1.26+.

- **`golangci_lint_fmt` formatter builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1244](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1244). Wraps `golangci-lint fmt`, the formatter half of golangci-lint, formatting only the changed files via `check_diff` (using `fmt --diff`) — separate from the existing `golangci_lint` builtin that runs the full linter.

- **`ls_lint` builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1238](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1238). Adds a builtin for [ls-lint](https://ls-lint.org), which enforces directory and filename naming conventions against `.ls-lint.yml`. Runs once per invocation. Implements proposal 3 of [#1234](https://github.com/jdx/hk/issues/1234).

- **`gitleaks_staged` builtin** (@jdx) [#1248](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1248). A new builtin that runs `gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged` to scan only the staged index, suited to pre-commit hooks.

- **Per-step `allow_failure`** (@jdx) [#1291](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1291). Steps can report a non-zero command exit without failing the overall hook, including conditional policies via expressions such as `env('KNOWN_BROKEN') == 'true'`. hk's own execution and configuration errors remain blocking, and allowed failures are surfaced in structured output.

- **gitleaks scan modes** (@jdx) [#1248](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1248). `Builtins.gitleaks` now explicitly scans the repository working tree rather than silently changing behavior when `{{files}}` expanded to multiple paths.
- **`gomod_tidy` now runs on `.go` changes** (@sahidvelji) [#1236](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1236). Broadened the glob to `**/*.go`, `**/go.mod`, and `**/go.sum` so the common drift (editing an import) is caught at commit time, and its `go.mod`/`go.sum` updates are now staged when triggered by a Go change (@jdx) [#1240](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1240).

{"body":"Excuse all my AI slop, I was trying to figure out why hk with subprojects was causing me some trouble.

The issue was that `hk fix --all` behaved differently in {repo-root}/ versus {repo-root}/{sub-project}, where the latter failed.  First is a summary, and the second is an attempt at a minimal viable reproducer. 

Thanks for your help!

---
Two related bugs in how a step's `dir` interacts with a subdirectory that has its own hk.pkl:

1. join_subdir only special-cased an empty dir as "no additional subpath" — a literal "." was concatenated as-is, producing "subdir/." instead of "subdir", which then fails to prefix-match real file paths.

2. Git::new always cds the whole process into the git work tree root on startup, regardless of where the discovered hk.pkl actually lives. A config found by walking up from a subdirectory (i.e. not merged in via a parent's `subprojects`) never got any directory scoping at all: every step ran against, and matched files from, the entire repo rather than its own directory.
---

Fixes the second with a new apply_implicit_root_dir, computed once right after loading the project config and before subprojects are merged in (those already scope themselves via merge_subproject).


 Setup:
  repo/
  ├── a.tf                          # tracked file at repo root
  └── hk.pkl

  hk.pkl:
  ```
  amends "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.56.1/hk@1.56.1#/Config.pkl"
  
  local linters = new Mapping<String, Step> {
      ["dot-dir"] {
          dir = "."
          glob = List("*.tf")
          check = "echo DOT_DIR_MATCHED: {{ files }}"
      }
      ["null-dir"] {
          glob = List("*.tf")
          check = "echo NULL_DIR_MATCHED: {{ files }}"
      }
  }

  hooks {
      ["check"] { steps = linters }
  }
```

  Run hk check --all with the real upstream v1.56.1 release binary:
  ```
  ❯ null-dir
    null-dir – 1 file – *.tf – echo NULL_DIR_MATCHED: a.tf
    null-dir – NULL_DIR_MATCHED: a.tf
  ✔ null-dir
  dot-dir never even appears — it silently matched 0 files and got dropped. null-dir (same config, just dir omitted) matches fine.
```

  Second bug, same root cause family — standalone subdir invocation:
  
  repo/
  ├── a.tf
  ├── sub/
  │   ├── a.tf
  │   └── hk.pkl        # no `dir` set, not listed in any parent's subprojects
  Run cd repo/sub && hk check --all with the real v1.56.1 binary: it matches both a.tf files (root's and sub's) — dir unset resolves to the git root, not to sub/, because
  hk.pkl was found by walking up rather than merged in via subprojects.

{"body":"Fixes the `HK_CHECK` bug found while reviewing the docs in #1316. Now that #1316 has merged, this is rebased onto `main` and contains only the fix.

## The bug

`Hook::run_type` read `env::HK_FIX` directly and consulted only `opts.check`, so two documented configuration sources did nothing at all:

- **`HK_CHECK` / `git config hk.check`** were declared in `settings.toml` and reported by `hk config dump`, but nothing read the resulting `check` setting. `HK_CHECK=1 hk fix` still ran fix commands, so anyone setting it in CI to get a report rather than fixes silently got modified files.
- **`git config hk.fix`** was inert for the same reason, since only the `HK_FIX` env var was ever consulted.

The setting plumbing was already correct — `hk config get check` returned `true` under `HK_CHECK=1`. Only the consumer was missing.

## The fix

Read the merged `check` and `fix` settings, which picks up the env and git layers with their existing precedence:

```rust
if opts.check {
    return RunType::Check;
}
if opts.fix {
    return RunType::Fix;
}
let settings = Settings::get();
if settings.check {
    return RunType::Check;
}
let fix = self.fix.unwrap_or(self.name == "fix");
if settings.fix && fix {
    RunType::Fix
} else {
    RunType::Check
}
```

Two decisions worth flagging:

- **Flags stay ahead of the settings.** `--check` and `--fix` are hook options rather than global flags, so they never reach the settings layer (`CLI_SNAPSHOT` carries only the global ones). They are handled first so a flag still outranks the env and git sources, preserving the documented CLI > env > git precedence.
- **`check` wins over `fix`** when both are enabled, since the safer reading of a contradictory configuration is to leave files alone.

`env::HK_FIX` has no remaining callers now that the setting supersedes it, so the static is dropped.

## Behavior

Everything below was verified against a scratch repo whose step echoes which command ran. Only the three bolded rows change.

| invocation | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hk fix` | fix | fix |
| **`HK_CHECK=1 hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| **`git config hk.check true` + `hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| **`git config hk.fix false` + `hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| `HK_FIX=0 hk fix` | check | check |
| `hk fix --check` | check | check |
| `HK_CHECK=1 hk fix --fix` | fix | fix |
| `HK_FIX=0 hk fix --fix` | fix | fix |
| `HK_CHECK=0` + `git config hk.check true` | fix | fix |
| `hk check` | check | check |
| `hk check --fix` | fix | fix |

## Tests

{"body":"Fixes the `HK_CHECK` bug found while reviewing the docs in #1316. Now that #1316 has merged, this is rebased onto `main` and contains only the fix.

`Hook::run_type` read `env::HK_FIX` directly and consulted only `opts.check`, so two documented configuration sources did nothing at all:

- **`HK_CHECK` / `git config hk.check`** were declared in `settings.toml` and reported by `hk config dump`, but nothing read the resulting `check` setting. `HK_CHECK=1 hk fix` still ran fix commands, so anyone setting it in CI to get a report rather than fixes silently got modified files.
- **`git config hk.fix`** was inert for the same reason, since only the `HK_FIX` env var was ever consulted.

The setting plumbing was already correct — `hk config get check` returned `true` under `HK_CHECK=1`. Only the consumer was missing.

## The fix

Read the merged `check` and `fix` settings, which picks up the env and git layers with their existing precedence:

```rust
if opts.check {
    return RunType::Check;
}
if opts.fix {
    return RunType::Fix;
}
let settings = Settings::get();
if settings.check {
    return RunType::Check;
}
let fix = self.fix.unwrap_or(self.name == "fix");
if settings.fix && fix {
    RunType::Fix
} else {
    RunType::Check
}
```

Two decisions worth flagging:

- **Flags stay ahead of the settings.** `--check` and `--fix` are hook options rather than global flags, so they never reach the settings layer (`CLI_SNAPSHOT` carries only the global ones). They are handled first so a flag still outranks the env and git sources, preserving the documented CLI > env > git precedence.
- **`check` wins over `fix`** when both are enabled, since the safer reading of a contradictory configuration is to leave files alone.

`env::HK_FIX` has no remaining callers now that the setting supersedes it, so the static is dropped.

## Behavior

Everything below was verified against a scratch repo whose step echoes which command ran. Only the three bolded rows change.

| invocation | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hk fix` | fix | fix |
| **`HK_CHECK=1 hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| **`git config hk.check true` + `hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| **`git config hk.fix false` + `hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| `HK_FIX=0 hk fix` | check | check |
| `hk fix --check` | check | check |
| `HK_CHECK=1 hk fix --fix` | fix | fix |
| `HK_FIX=0 hk fix --fix` | fix | fix |
| `HK_CHECK=0` + `git config hk.check true` | fix | fix |
| `hk check` | check | check |
| `hk check --fix` | fix | fix |

`test/check_fix_mode.bats` covers the two fixed sources, their precedence against the flags and each other, and the unchanged defaults. This release seeds hk with an embedded Pkl package so matching-version configs validate offline on a cold cache, adds templated `dir` support for workspace-aware steps, and lands a new `check_after_diff` mechanism that lets partial fixers (like ShellCheck) apply what they can while still reporting what they cannot. It also brings several new Go and lint builtins plus a batch of correctness fixes for Go linters, gitleaks, workspace paths, Windows shims, and stashing.

## Added

- **Embedded matching-version Pkl package** (@sahidvelji) [#1218](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1218). hk now ships the Pkl package built for its own version and seeds `HK_PKL_CACHE_DIR` with it before evaluating `hk.pkl`, so a config pinned to that version validates with no network round trip on a cold cache — a fresh clone, CI runner, new container, or upgrade. Cached content always wins over the embedded copy, and other versions are fetched as before. Set `HK_PKL_EMBEDDED=0` to disable seeding. Addresses [discussion #1216](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1216).

- **Templated `dir` through Tera** (@sahidvelji) [#1219](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1219). A step's `dir` is now rendered through Tera, so a workspace-aware step can point its working directory at the workspace it was matched for instead of prefixing every command with `cd {{workspace}} && ...`. The eight workspace-aware builtins (the Go ones plus `cargo_deny`) drop their `cd` prefix as a result. Literal `dir` values are unaffected.

  ```pkl
  ["go-vet"] {
    glob = "**/*.go"
    workspace_indicator = "go.mod"
    dir = "{{workspace}}"
    check = "go vet ./..."
  }
  ```

- **`check_after_diff` for partial fixers** (@jdx) [#1243](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1243). New opt-in step setting that reruns `check` on the original file batch after a `check_diff` patch applies, so non-fixable findings stay visible instead of being masked by a clean apply. Requires both `check` and `check_diff` to be defined. This underpins ShellCheck's new fixer and other partial fixers.

- **ShellCheck autofix via `check_diff`** (@sahidvelji) [#1237](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1237). `shellcheck` now applies the fixes it can via `--format=diff`, and thanks to `check_after_diff` a file with both fixable and non-fixable findings is fixed and still fails on what remains. Implements proposal 2 of [#1234](https://github.com/jdx/hk/issues/1234).

- **`go_fix` builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1224](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1224). Wraps Go's `go fix` (the Go 1.26+ analyzer-driven modernizer) — `interface{}` → `any`, `sort.Slice` → `slices.Sort`, `wg.Add`/`go`/`wg.Done` → `wg.Go`, and more. `check_diff` runs `go fix -diff ./...` and hk applies the patch directly. Requires Go 1.26+.

- **`golangci_lint_fmt` formatter builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1244](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1244). Wraps `golangci-lint fmt`, the formatter half of golangci-lint, formatting only the changed files via `check_diff` (using `fmt --diff`) — separate from the existing `golangci_lint` builtin that runs the full linter.

- **`ls_lint` builtin** (@sahidvelji) [#1238](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1238). Adds a builtin for [ls-lint](https://ls-lint.org), which enforces directory and filename naming conventions against `.ls-lint.yml`. Runs once per invocation. Implements proposal 3 of [#1234](https://github.com/jdx/hk/issues/1234).

- **`gitleaks_staged` builtin** (@jdx) [#1248](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1248). A new builtin that runs `gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged` to scan only the staged index, suited to pre-commit hooks.

- **Per-step `allow_failure`** (@jdx) [#1291](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1291). Steps can report a non-zero command exit without failing the overall hook, including conditional policies via expressions such as `env('KNOWN_BROKEN') == 'true'`. hk's own execution and configuration errors remain blocking, and allowed failures are surfaced in structured output.

## Fixed

- **Go linters that reported success on bad code** (@sahidvelji) [#1225](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1225). `go_imports`, `go_lines`, `revive`, and `go_fumpt` silently passed in check mode even with real findings; they now take their exit code correctly. `gomod_tidy` could not run outside the repo root and is now scoped like the other Go builtins.
- **gitleaks scan modes** (@jdx) [#1248](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1248). `Builtins.gitleaks` now explicitly scans the repository working tree rather than silently changing behavior when `{{files}}` expanded to multiple paths.
- **`gomod_tidy` now runs on `.go` changes** (@sahidvelji) [#1236](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1236). Broadened the glob to `**/*.go`, `**/go.mod`, and `**/go.sum` so the common drift (editing an import) is caught at commit time, and its `go.mod`/`go.sum` updates are now staged when triggered by a Go change (@jdx) [#1240](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1240).
- **Partial diff fixes no longer pass silently** (@jdx) [#1245](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1245). Enabled `check_after_diff` for `rumdl`, `ryl`, `ryl_markdown`, `zizmor`, and `pinact_v3`, so remaining violations surface after hk applies each partial patch.
- **Workspace paths in literal `dir` steps** (@jdx) [#1242](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1242). `{{workspace}}` and `{{workspace_indicator}}` are now rendered relative to a literal step directory, preventing duplicated paths like `ui/ui/tsconfig.json` in subprojects. Addresses [discussion #1233](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1233).
- **Windows command shims** (@jdx) [#1221](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1221). Structured `argv` steps now resolve `.cmd`/`.bat` targets (including npm `node_modules/.bin` shims) via the effective `PATH`/`PATHEXT` and run them through `cmd.exe` with argument-boundary-preserving escaping. Fixes [discussion #1220](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1220).
- **Empty pathspec stashes** (@jdx) [#1283](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1283). Pre-commit runs no longer reset the index and leave an orphaned stash when a path-limited stash has no HEAD-to-worktree diff (e.g. mode-only staged changes). Addresses [discussion #1281](https://github.com/jdx/hk/discussions/1281).

{"body":"Excuse all my AI slop, I was trying to figure out why hk with subprojects was causing me some trouble.

The issue was that `hk fix --all` behaved differently in {repo-root}/ versus {repo-root}/{sub-project}, where the latter failed.  First is a summary, and the second is an attempt at a minimal viable reproducer. 

Thanks for your help!

---
Two related bugs in how a step's `dir` interacts with a subdirectory that has its own hk.pkl:

1. join_subdir only special-cased an empty dir as "no additional subpath" — a literal "." was concatenated as-is, producing "subdir/." instead of "subdir", which then fails to prefix-match real file paths.

2. Git::new always cds the whole process into the git work tree root on startup, regardless of where the discovered hk.pkl actually lives. A config found by walking up from a subdirectory (i.e. not merged in via a parent's `subprojects`) never got any directory scoping at all: every step ran against, and matched files from, the entire repo rather than its own directory.
---

Fixes the second with a new apply_implicit_root_dir, computed once right after loading the project config and before subprojects are merged in (those already scope themselves via merge_subproject).


 Setup:
  repo/
  ├── a.tf                          # tracked file at repo root
  └── hk.pkl

  hk.pkl:
  ```
  amends "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v1.56.1/hk@1.56.1#/Config.pkl"
  
  local linters = new Mapping<String, Step> {
      ["dot-dir"] {
          dir = "."
          glob = List("*.tf")
          check = "echo DOT_DIR_MATCHED: {{ files }}"
      }
      ["null-dir"] {
          glob = List("*.tf")
          check = "echo NULL_DIR_MATCHED: {{ files }}"
      }
  }

  hooks {
      ["check"] { steps = linters }
  }
```

  Run hk check --all with the real upstream v1.56.1 release binary:
  ```
  ❯ null-dir
    null-dir – 1 file – *.tf – echo NULL_DIR_MATCHED: a.tf
    null-dir – NULL_DIR_MATCHED: a.tf
  ✔ null-dir
  dot-dir never even appears — it silently matched 0 files and got dropped. null-dir (same config, just dir omitted) matches fine.
```

  Second bug, same root cause family — standalone subdir invocation:
  
  repo/
  ├── a.tf
  ├── sub/
  │   ├── a.tf
  │   └── hk.pkl        # no `dir` set, not listed in any parent's subprojects
  Run cd repo/sub && hk check --all with the real v1.56.1 binary: it matches both a.tf files (root's and sub's) — dir unset resolves to the git root, not to sub/, because
  hk.pkl was found by walking up rather than merged in via subprojects.

{"body":"Fixes the `HK_CHECK` bug found while reviewing the docs in #1316. Now that #1316 has merged, this is rebased onto `main` and contains only the fix.

## The bug

`Hook::run_type` read `env::HK_FIX` directly and consulted only `opts.check`, so two documented configuration sources did nothing at all:

- **`HK_CHECK` / `git config hk.check`** were declared in `settings.toml` and reported by `hk config dump`, but nothing read the resulting `check` setting. `HK_CHECK=1 hk fix` still ran fix commands, so anyone setting it in CI to get a report rather than fixes silently got modified files.
- **`git config hk.fix`** was inert for the same reason, since only the `HK_FIX` env var was ever consulted.

The setting plumbing was already correct — `hk config get check` returned `true` under `HK_CHECK=1`. Only the consumer was missing.

## The fix

Read the merged `check` and `fix` settings, which picks up the env and git layers with their existing precedence:

```rust
if opts.check {
    return RunType::Check;
}
if opts.fix {
    return RunType::Fix;
}
let settings = Settings::get();
if settings.check {
    return RunType::Check;
}
let fix = self.fix.unwrap_or(self.name == "fix");
if settings.fix && fix {
    RunType::Fix
} else {
    RunType::Check
}
```

Two decisions worth flagging:

- **Flags stay ahead of the settings.** `--check` and `--fix` are hook options rather than global flags, so they never reach the settings layer (`CLI_SNAPSHOT` carries only the global ones). They are handled first so a flag still outranks the env and git sources, preserving the documented CLI > env > git precedence.
- **`check` wins over `fix`** when both are enabled, since the safer reading of a contradictory configuration is to leave files alone.

`env::HK_FIX` has no remaining callers now that the setting supersedes it, so the static is dropped.

## Behavior

Everything below was verified against a scratch repo whose step echoes which command ran. Only the three bolded rows change.

| invocation | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hk fix` | fix | fix |
| **`HK_CHECK=1 hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| **`git config hk.check true` + `hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| **`git config hk.fix false` + `hk fix`** | **fix** | **check** |
| `HK_FIX=0 hk fix` | check | check |
| `hk fix --check` | check | check |
| `HK_CHECK=1 hk fix --fix` | fix | fix |
| `HK_FIX=0 hk fix --fix` | fix | fix |
| `HK_CHECK=0` + `git config hk.check true` | fix | fix |
| `hk check` | check | check |
| `hk check --fix` | fix | fix |

## Tests

`test/check_fix_mode.bats` covers the two fixed sources, their precedence against the flags and each other, and the unchanged defaults. I confirmed the tests actually guard the fix by reverting the change and re-running: the `HK_CHECK`, `hk.check`, and `hk.fix` cases fail, and the other seven pass either way as regression cover for the refactor.

Full suite: 1305 bats tests and 292 Rust tests pass. The only failures in my environment are missing local tools (`git-lfs`, `go`, `ktlint`, and similar for the builtin tool tests), which fail identically on `main`.

## Docs

The `HK_CHECK` entry now describes the working behavior, its precedence against the flags and `HK_FIX`, and the `git config hk.check` equivalent. It also states that selecting check commands is not a guarantee of an unchanged worktree, since hk does not constrain what a project's check command does — the same qualification applied to the `check` and `fix` entries in `settings.toml`, one of which still called check commands "read-only".

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5; version: unavailable.*

{"body":"Fixes #1294. `pkl/Builtins.pkl` is generated and gitignored, and `build-binaries` invokes `cargo`/`cross` directly rather than through a mise task, so `build.rs` never saw it and every released binary shipped an empty embedded package — silently falling back to the network. `test/pkl_embedded_package.bats` passed throughout because `ci-impl.yml` runs `pkl:gen` before it; the gap was release-only.

Two calls worth flagging:

- `MBX_DISABLE=1` on the job — mise-action puts mise's shims on PATH, where the `cargo` shim routes through the `[wrappers.cargo]` mbx wrapper from #1300. Adding mise here just for `pkl:gen` would otherwise reroute release builds as a side effect.
- `HK_REQUIRE_EMBEDDED_PKL` is repeated in the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` block as well as `[build.env]` because I couldn't confirm whether cross 0.2.5 merges the two passthrough lists or lets the target one win.

Verified locally that a build without `pkl/Builtins.pkl` fails under the new guard and still falls back without it.

{"body":"The `pinact` and `pinact_update` builtins' glob `List(".github/workflows/*", "*/action.*")` never matches a root-level `action.yml`/`action.yaml` (standalone action repositories), because the pattern requires a `/` before `action.`.

pinact's own default discovery does include root action metadata (see `defaultWorkflowPatterns` in [`pkg/controller/run/list_workflows.go`](https://github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact/blob/main/pkg/controller/run/list_workflows.go): `action.yml`, `action.yaml`, and one-to-three-level-deep variants). Under hk, `{{files}}` replaces pinact's own discovery, so the step glob is the gate — this change restores parity for both builtins (they define the same glob independently; `pinact_v3`/`pinact_update_v3` inherit it).

Notes:
- hk builds step globs without `literal_separator` (`src/glob.rs`), so `*` already crosses `/` and nested files like `.github/actions/setup/action.yml` matched before this change; root was the only gap. `**/action.*` covers root and all depths.
- `types = List("yaml")` composes with AND, so the widened glob still only selects YAML.
- No test added: `StepTest` passes `files` explicitly, so glob selection is not exercised by `hk test`.

## Content errors

**Wrong config precedence.** The `hk config` help text and the output of `hk config sources` both placed user config above git config and project config. `Config::merge_from_hkrc` applies project values over hkrc values, and `Settings` applies layers as defaults < pkl < git < env < cli, so the documented order was wrong in two places. **Broken example.** The `commit-msg` example in `docs/hooks.md` used `grep -q '^(fix|feat|chore):'` with a trailing `|| exit 1`. - `hk config get` help listed a hard-coded key set that no longer matches `SETTINGS_META`; it now points at `hk config dump`.

{"body":"Fixes #1294. `pkl/Builtins.pkl` is generated and gitignored, and `build-binaries` invokes `cargo`/`cross` directly rather than through a mise task, so `build.rs` never saw it and every released binary shipped an empty embedded package — silently falling back to the network. `test/pkl_embedded_package.bats` passed throughout because `ci-impl.yml` runs `pkl:gen` before it; the gap was release-only.

Two calls worth flagging:

- `MBX_DISABLE=1` on the job — mise-action puts mise's shims on PATH, where the `cargo` shim routes through the `[wrappers.cargo]` mbx wrapper from #1300. Adding mise here just for `pkl:gen` would otherwise reroute release builds as a side effect.
- `HK_REQUIRE_EMBEDDED_PKL` is repeated in the `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` block as well as `[build.env]` because I couldn't confirm whether cross 0.2.5 merges the two passthrough lists or lets the target one win.

Verified locally that a build without `pkl/Builtins.pkl` fails under the new guard and still falls back without it.

## Content errors

**Wrong config precedence.** The `hk config` help text and the output of `hk config sources` both placed user config above git config and project config. `Config::merge_from_hkrc` applies project values over hkrc values, and `Settings` applies layers as defaults < pkl < git < env < cli, so the documented order was wrong in two places. Both now report CLI > env > git (local) > git (global) > project > user config > defaults, matching `docs/configuration.md`.

**Broken example.** The `commit-msg` example in `docs/hooks.md` used `grep -q '^(fix|feat|chore):'` with a trailing `|| exit 1`. Basic `grep` does not interpret `|` alternation, so the example only matched a literal parenthesized string. Changed to `grep -Eq`, and dropped the redundant `|| exit 1`.

**Invented `HK_DISPLAY_SKIP_REASONS` values.** The docs listed `all` and `none`, which `SkipReason::should_display` does not implement (it does a plain membership test), and omitted six of the nine real reasons. Replaced with the reasons the code actually emits.

- **Standalone subprojects stay in scope** ([@thespags](https://github.com/thespags)) [#1290](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1290). Running hk from a subdirectory with its own `hk.pkl` no longer causes that config to match unrelated files from the repository root. Literal `dir = "."` steps are scoped correctly as well.
- **Check/fix settings select the right command** ([@jdx](https://github.com/jdx)) [#1318](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1318). `HK_CHECK`, `git config hk.check`, and `git config hk.fix` now affect run-type selection as documented. Explicit flags retain highest precedence, and check mode wins when configuration is contradictory so hk leaves files unchanged.
- **pinact sees root action metadata** ([@risu729](https://github.com/risu729)) [#1321](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1321). The `pinact` and `pinact_update` builtins now include a repository-root `action.yml` or `action.yaml`, not only workflow and nested action files.
- **Release binaries embed the Pkl package again** ([@sahidvelji](https://github.com/sahidvelji)) [#1299](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1299). Release builds now generate the gitignored builtin package before compilation and fail if it is absent, preventing a supposedly self-contained binary from silently requiring a network fetch.
- **Release publication targets the source repository** ([@jdx](https://github.com/jdx)) [#1292](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1292), avoiding accidental reliance on the caller's current repository context.

## Documentation

- Corrected configuration precedence, check/fix environment-variable behavior, supported skip reasons, stash descriptions, and several CLI examples; added missing help for hook subcommands and options [#1316](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1316).
- Clarified that Lefthook provides partial pre-commit stash handling while leaving untracked files visible [#1297](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1297).
- Added Open Graph and search metadata, including the initial social preview image [#1324](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1324) [#1327](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1327).

## Release and CI

Release and performance infrastructure was updated throughout this cycle: hk adopted the mr-boxington cargo shim and dedicated performance runners, restored and refined remote build caching, updated runner images and action dependencies, added conventional-commit enforcement, and introduced signed packslip generation for release artifacts.

## New Contributors

- [@thespags](https://github.com/thespags) made their first contribution in [#1290](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1290).
- [@illesnagy1](https://github.com/illesnagy1) made their first contribution in [#1302](https://github.com/jdx/hk/pull/1302).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/hk/compare/v1.57.0...v1.58.0

## 💚 Sponsor hk

hk is maintained by [@jdx](https://github.com/jdx), an open source developer at [**entire.io**](https://entire.io/), the title sponsor of his open source work.

If hk speeds up your pre-commit loop or makes linting less painful, please consider becoming an [individual or company sponsor](https://jdx.dev/sponsors.html). Your support funds ongoing development and helps keep hk fast, free, and independent.
